newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: RUSSIAN-SLOVAK GAS DELIVERY DEAL READY - RUSSIAN PM.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN-SLOVAK GAS DELIVERY DEAL READY - RUSSIAN PM.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, on the first day of an official three-day visit, said on Monday a long-term gas delivery contract with Slovakia was ready to be signed.

"We are ready to sign an agreement on deliveries and schedules and this will be a long-term one," Chernomyrdin told a news conference after a two-hour session with his Slovak counterpart Vladimir Meciar.

Chernomyrdin added that his first round of talks with Meciar, which concentrated on economic cooperation and finalisng several accords the two are due to sign on Tuesday, included a treaty on the construction of a further transit pipeline.
Slovakia is a major transporter of Russian natural gas to western Europe, supplying some 80 billion cubic metres annually.

Russian gas imports also cover the entire annual Slovak domestic consumption of around six billion cubic metres. Russia's Gazprom pays for the transfer of supplies by supplying about two-thirds of this total.
Chernomyrdin did not say anything about the signing of a planned joint-venture between Gazprom and Slovak gas distributor SPP, which local media reported on Monday as having been delayed.

"Talks on the contract on the creation of a joint-venture are still on going but the two sides will sign only a letter of intent on a future contract," SPP Director Jan Ducky was quoted by the daily Narodna Obroda as saying.

Ducky gave no reason for the postponement of the contract, which was part of a series of economic agreements between the two countries to be signed by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin who began a three-day visit on Monday.
The joint-venture, which will manage deliveries above the contracted quotas of Russian gas to western Europe, was one of the most important items on Chernomyrdin's agenda.
